in_english.name: Hawwaa'
in_english.meaning: Hawwaa' is the name of the first woman created by God, also known as Eve.
in_english.long_meaning: Hawwaa' is the name of the first woman created by God, according to the Quran and the Bible. She is the wife of Adam and the first woman on earth. The name Hawwaa' is derived from the Arabic root 'h-w-w', which means to create or bring into being. In Islamic tradition, Hawwaa' is seen as a symbol of femininity and creativity. She is also associated with the concept of paradise and the Garden of Eden. In the Quran, Hawwaa' is described as a companion to Adam and a partner in his creation. The name Hawwaa' is also used to refer to the first human beings, Adam and Hawwaa', who were created by God. In Islamic theology, Hawwaa' is considered a role model for women and is often cited as an example of a pious and obedient companion. The name Hawwaa' is also used in various contexts to refer to women who are virtuous, pious, and obedient to God's commandments. In modern times, the name Hawwaa' has become popular in many Muslim countries, particularly in the Middle East and North Africa.
